meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have about twenty-five minutes before a client call, and I'd like to know why my son found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. I'm writing that down. Now tell me what you based it on, Hale.
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
Okay, Hale. You said you wrote it down the same day, so show me the note with the date on it. And one question asked on the spot doesn't tell me who wrote the essay.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.

An outline from October 15 and an essay due October 29, Hale. Students change their argument in two weeks; that's called revising. Show me the outline, and the note from November 2, and I'll read them myself.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

You're offering me a rewrite and you still haven't put one page in front of me, Hale. The zero comes off first, and I want your terms in writing before Thursday, not Friday afternoon after it's done. Show me the outline and your note, then we'll talk about terms.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, your terms in writing before Thursday, and the outline and your November 2 note put in front of me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, with the zero still in place and nothing agreed.
What moved her: "I put the zero in before calling you" earned a flat "Okay" and a small step toward listening, because you owned it in one sentence.
What cost ground: "Here's my offer" came before you had shown her a single document, so she kept demanding paper instead of weighing terms.
Try next time: after she asked to see the outline and the November 2 note, put them in front of her before you offered the rewrite.
